# A guardrails record fits the store, or its check fails

Status: the maintainer ruled, on [issue #605](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/605), that a guardrails record must fit the store's 4 MiB record limit, and that one which cannot fit even with every finding's detail left out fails closed. Trimming the check's own findings, rather than only the exported record, is the builder's choice, which the coordinator agreed on 2026-11-20; it is not a ruling.

The port, `RecordStore`, promises what rule 3 says and no more. `add` checks each record whole. `list` checks envelopes only and leaves payloads to the caller's `RecordSet`, so a record set aside as untrusted cannot stop a listing. Both adapters validate a whole batch before they write any of it, but the port does not require that, since rule 3 lets a batch land in part. The conformance suite asserts only that a refused record never lists and that a repeat of the rest completes the batch. Every adapter refuses a record whose canonical bytes pass `recordLimit`, 4 MiB of UTF-8, with `invalidRecord`, through `SharedRecord.storable()`, and measures the whole batch before it writes any of it; the conformance suite holds every adapter to that, at the limit and a byte past it. The relay takes a file up to the same limit, so the head's job never hands over a record no store keeps. A ruling on the limit changes that one number. A check record's sightings get the limit less `envelopeAllowance`, 4 KiB for the envelope and the check's result, as `SightingBudget.checkRecord`. Problem: a head that changes 1,500 workspace manifests, each naming twenty long scripts, writes a guardrails record of about 5 MB, and the store refuses it. Solution: `fit(findings)` walks the findings in ID order and keeps each one's detail while the full findings so far and the shortest form of every later one fit. Each later finding is `abridged(note)`: What becomes its fixed headline, unless its own What is shorter in UTF-8 bytes, Why here becomes "Melian left out the detail for N more files to keep this record under its limit; `git diff` shows those files.", with N the files those findings name, and its ID, rule, severity, resolution, place, snippet, trigger and What to do stay. A finding that abridging would not make smaller, because its Why here is shorter than the note, keeps its detail, so no finding grows. The same findings give the same bytes.
